title: Stele of Hammurabi, with 'Code of Laws' (Fig. IX.3)
creator: Unknown photographer (book illustration)
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).
original_holder: Lewis Spence, Myths and Legends of Babylonia and Assyria (London: Harrap, 1916), fig. IX.3; the stele itself is in the Louvre
caption: The diorite stele of Hammurabi as photographed in the Louvre. At the top the king stands before the seated sun god Shamash; the law text runs below. Hammurabi's own debt-cancelling edicts are known from other documents, not from this stele.

title: The Rosetta Stone
creator: Unknown (British Museum publication)
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).
original_holder: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Rosetta Stone (London: British Museum, 1913)
caption: The Memphis decree of 196 BC, inscribed in hieroglyphic, demotic and Greek. Among its clauses, Ptolemy V remits debts and arrears owed to the crown and releases prisoners. This is a printed reproduction from a British Museum booklet, not a modern photograph.

title: Descartes (Fig. 53)
creator: Unknown engraver, after a 17th-century portrait type

original_holder: Oliver Lodge, Pioneers of Science (London: Macmillan, 1893), fig. 53
caption: René Descartes in an engraved oval portrait reproduced in a Victorian history of science. It is a later engraving after a portrait made decades after the three dreams of November 1619 that he recorded and Baillet retold.

caption: Girolamo Cardano in profile, with the legend giving his age as 68. The book reproduces a portrait from his lifetime; this copy is small (326 px wide).

title: Hildegard receiving the light from heaven (Plate I)
creator: Rupertsberg scriptorium (miniature); unknown photographer

caption: The opening miniature of the Rupertsberg Scivias: tongues of fire descend onto Hildegard as she writes on wax tablets, while the monk Volmar looks in from the side. The codex itself was lost in 1945, so plates like this one help to show how it looked.

title: Birth: the arrival and trials of the soul (Plate XIX)

caption: Scivias I.4 as painted in the Rupertsberg codex: a soul comes down as a bright form into a child in the womb, while people below carry vessels. The scenes on the right show the soul's trials. The original codex was lost in 1945.

title: The days of creation and the fall of man (Plate XXII)
creator: Rupertsberg scriptorium (miniature); unknown photographer

caption: Scivias I.2: a starry mass falls from a dark disc of light, the fallen angels, and a serpent breathes on Adam and Eve below. The plate is a monochrome photograph of the lost manuscript.

title: The vision of the Trinity (Plate XXIII)
creator: Rupertsberg scriptorium (miniature); unknown photographer

caption: Scivias II.2: a sapphire-blue human figure stands inside rings of silver light and red fire. The text describes a single 'living light' in which the three are seen together.

title: The heavenly city (Plate XXV)
creator: Rupertsberg scriptorium (miniature); unknown photographer

title: The Election, Plate I: An Election Entertainment
creator: William Hogarth (after); later re-engraving for a book edition
why_public_domain: A 19th-century book illustration; long out of copyright everywhere.
original_holder: John Ireland and John Nichols, Hogarth's Works, vol. 2 (London: Chatto & Windus, 19th century)
caption: A Whig election dinner in uproar. On the floor at lower right lies a captured Tory placard reading 'Give us our Eleven Days', a satirical nod to the 1752 calendar change. This is a reduced later copy of the print, so the placard is hard to read at this size.

title: The Julian calendar, reformed by Gregory XIII
creator: George Nichols Packer
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).
original_holder: George Nichols Packer, Our Calendar (Corning, NY, 1890-1893)
caption: A teaching diagram from an 1890s American handbook. It contrasts Caesar's 445-day 'last year of confusion' in 46 BC with Gregory XIII's October 1582, when ten days were dropped and the 5th was followed by the 15th.

title: Frankenstein, frontispiece to the 1831 edition

caption: The creature wakes on the floor of the laboratory while Victor flees through the door. The engraved caption quotes the novel: 'By the glimmer of the half-extinguished light, I saw the dull, yellow eye of the creature open'. It appeared in the revised 1831 edition, the one with Mary Shelley's new introduction about the summer at Diodati.

title: Frankenstein, engraved title page of the 1831 edition

title: Down House
creator: Unknown engraver (book illustration)
why_public_domain: A 19th-century book illustration; long out of copyright everywhere.
original_holder: Francis Darwin (ed.), The Life and Letters of Charles Darwin, vol. 1 (London: John Murray, 1887)
caption: The Darwins' house at Downe in Kent, where they moved in September 1842 and where the 1842 sketch and 1844 essay of the theory were written. The engraving shows the house as it looked decades later, with the bay added in the 1850s.

title: Diagram of embryonic development

caption: The only diagram in the anonymous Vestiges: fish, reptile, bird and mammal share a line of development before branching off at different points. The book's success in 1844-45, and the attacks on it, were one reason Darwin kept his own theory private.

title: Tesla's rotating-field motor and generator (Fig. 9)
creator: Nikola Tesla (diagram); unknown draughtsman
why_public_domain: A 19th-century book illustration; long out of copyright everywhere.
original_holder: Thomas Commerford Martin, The Inventions, Researches and Writings of Nikola Tesla (New York: The Electrical Engineer, 1894), ch. III, fig. 9
caption: A figure from Tesla's 1888 AIEE paper 'A New System of Alternate Current Motors and Transformers', as reprinted by Martin. A generator with collector rings (right) feeds two out-of-step currents to a ring motor (left), whose field rotates. Tesla later said the idea came to him in Budapest in 1882 while reciting Goethe at sunset.

title: A ring wound for a rotating field (Fig. 10)
creator: Nikola Tesla (diagram); unknown draughtsman

caption: A laminated iron ring wound with coils and led out by four wires: the two-circuit field ring that Tesla's 1888 paper and patents describe. The drawing comes from Martin's 1894 reprint, not from the patent sheets.

title: Jerusalem, from the Mount of Olives

caption: The walled Old City seen from the east, with the Dome of the Rock behind the eastern wall. It was painted about half a century before 1948, when the city was divided along lines that ran just outside these walls.

title: The Temple Area and the Mount of Olives, from Mount Zion

caption: Rooftops of the Old City looking east from Mount Zion to the Haram al-Sharif and the Mount of Olives. Mount Zion and the Jewish Quarter below it were front lines in 1948. Painted about 1900.

title: Sketch map of country round Jerusalem
creator: H. O. Lock (book map)
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).

caption: A 1919 sketch map of the 1917 operations around Jerusalem. It shows the single road and railway climbing from the coast past Latrun and Bab el-Wad into the hills, the route that the 1948 convoys fought to keep open. It is a First World War map shown for context, not a 1948 document.

caption: Nixon's official portrait from his first term. It was not taken at the televised address of 15 August 1971 in which he closed the gold window.

title: Dr. C. G. Jung
creator: Unknown photographer
why_public_domain: Published before 1929; long out of copyright (public domain in the US, and the creators died more than 70 years ago).
